title: Etale local equations of nodal curves over a DVR
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $k$ its residue field, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose every nonempty geometric fibre is reduced of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed geometric fibre point over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For every point $x\in X_k$ there are an etale extension of DVRs $R\hookrightarrow R'$, a scheme $U$, a point $x'\in U$, and etale morphisms $p:U\to X$ and $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, compatible with the structural maps to $S$, with $p(x')=x$, where
$$ A=R'[u,v]/(uv)\quad\text{or}\quad A=R'[u,v]/(uv-\pi'^n),\qquad n\geq0,$$
and $\pi'$ is a uniformizer of $R'$. The map $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is the composite through $q$, and $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Polynomial rings are [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. No properness, connectedness, excellence or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, statement; nodal hypotheses expanded using curves.tex Tag 0C5A.

proof.text: First check the geometric-fibre hypothesis needed for [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model]. Local finite presentation gives finite-presentation affine charts over $R$ (a finite algebra presentation in each chart). A DVR is Noetherian by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and those charts, and their affine geometric fibres over $\Omega$, are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. A nonclosed point of a reduced pure one-dimensional geometric fibre is a generic point of an irreducible component: any proper specialization chain has length at most one. On a finite-presentation affine geometric-fibre chart $C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, all further geometric fibres are reduced by the original hypotheses, and flatness is automatic over a field. Thus [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] says that these generic points are smooth. Consequently every nonsmooth geometric-fibre point is closed and has exactly the completed local ring required in the cited nodal-model statement. This checks its condition at all points, rather than just at the closed points specified in our hypotheses.

source.place: Tags 0C59/0C5A, lemma-nodal-family and definition-nodal-family; varieties.tex Tag 056V, lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open

proof.text: Suppose first that $f$ is smooth at $x$. On the smooth locus the fibre dimension at $x$ is $1$: compute it after an algebraic closure of the residue field using [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change], where the fibre is a pure one-dimensional curve. Equivalently use the equidimensional-fibre formulation of relative dimension in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The locally constant dimension function of [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] allows a smooth neighbourhood of $x$ of pure relative dimension $1$. Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] with $d=1$ and then [lem-sc-standard-smooth-etale-polynomial-chart] to obtain an affine open $T\subset X$ containing $x$ and an etale $S$-map $e:T\to\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. The base affine neighbourhood supplied by the first lemma contains the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence equals $S$: any open containing the closed point of a local spectrum contains every prime. The composite to $S$ is $f|_T$, by the composite identity in the polynomial-chart lemma.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, smooth case; morphisms.tex Tags 02FY, 02G1, 054L (lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space)

proof.text: In the residue field of $e(x)$, either $t$ is nonzero, or $t=0$ and $t+1$ is nonzero. In the latter case replace $t$ by $t+1$ (an $R$-coordinate automorphism, inverse $t\mapsto t-1$). Restrict $T$ to $U=e^{-1}(D(t))$; this is an open neighbourhood of $x$ and the restricted map $U\to D(t)$ is the base change of $e$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The inclusion $p:U\hookrightarrow X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). The explicit ring isomorphism $R[u,v]/(uv-1)\cong R[t,t^{-1}]$, $u\mapsto t$, $v\mapsto t^{-1}$, with inverse $t\mapsto u$, identifies $D(t)$ with the desired model. Take $R\prime=R$, $n=0$, and $x\prime=x$ viewed in $U$. This includes generic points of the special fibre and all residue characteristics.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, smooth case and the identification D(u)=Spec R[u,v]/(uv-1)

proof.text: Now suppose $f$ is not smooth at $x$. Step 1 checks precisely the geometric hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model], and flatness and local finite presentation are assumptions. Apply that node to obtain $V\to S$, a function $h$ on $V$, etale maps $U\to X$ and $U\to W=\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h)$ over $S$, and $x\prime\in U$ over $x$. Put $v$ equal to the image of $x\prime$ in $V$; its image in $S$ is the closed point since $x\in X_k$. Choose an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset V$ containing $v$, and denote its prime by $\mathfrak q$. Its structural map to $S$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), and $\mathfrak q$ contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-dvr-principal-neighbourhood] to find $b\notin\mathfrak q$ for which $V_1=D(b)=\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$, $R\prime=B[1/b]$, is a DVR with injective local etale structural map from $R$.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, singular case, second and third proof paragraphs; curves.tex Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family

proof.text: Replace $U$ by $U_1=U\times_VV_1$ and $W$ by $W_1=W\times_VV_1$. Because $v\in V_1$, the chosen $x\prime$ is still a point of $U_1$. The map $U_1\to U$ is an open immersion; composing with $U\to X$ remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2). The map $U_1\to W_1$ is the base change of $U\to W$ and is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). If $h\prime$ denotes the restriction of $h$ to $V_1$, then $W_1=\operatorname{Spec}(R\prime[u,v]/(uv-h\prime))$: tensor the polynomial presentation along the restriction map, which sends the relation $uv-h$ to $uv-h\prime$. Every triangle to $S$ still commutes, since both maps were restricted along the same map $V_1\to V$.

source.place: Tag 0CDD, lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal, restriction to Spec R′ and fourth proof paragraph

proof.text:
Choose a uniformizer $\pi\prime$ of the DVR $R\prime$. If $h\prime=0$, the displayed ring in step 5 is already $R\prime[u,v]/(uv)$, so take this first model. If $h\prime\ne0$, [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] gives $h\prime=\epsilon(\pi\prime)^n$ with $\epsilon\in(R\prime)^\times$ and $n\ge0$; its hypotheses hold because a DVR is a Noetherian local domain with a nonzero principal maximal ideal, as recorded in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Normalize the coordinates by $u_0=\epsilon^{-1}u$, $v_0=v$. More explicitly the $R\prime$-algebra map
$$R\prime[u_0,v_0]/(u_0v_0-(\pi\prime)^n)\longrightarrow R\prime[u,v]/(uv-h\prime),\quad u_0\longmapsto\epsilon^{-1}u,\ v_0\longmapsto v$$
is well-defined because $\epsilon^{-1}uv=(\pi\prime)^n$, and its inverse sends $u\mapsto\epsilon u_0$, $v\mapsto v_0$. Composing the map of step 5 with the resulting $R\prime$-scheme isomorphism gives $q$ to the second model; local finite presentation, flatness and unramifiedness defining etaleness [def-weil-etale-morphism] are preserved under this identification of the target. The structural map $U_1\to\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$ is unchanged by this $R\prime$-isomorphism. Thus $p,q,x\prime,R\prime$ satisfy every clause. The zero parameter covers persistent nodes and $n=0$ was already allowed in the smooth case.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-9422b74eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's six steps against Stacks models.tex 0CDD, both branches. Step 1 shows that every non-closed point of a geometric fibre is a generic point and is smooth by lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth, so every hypothesis of the 0CBY nodal chart holds. Smooth branch: the étale chart to R[t] has base open equal to S because it contains the closed point; restricting to D(t) or D(t+1) gives the n=0 model with R'=R. Singular branch: the 0CBY chart, an affine V0 étale over S, then the new principal-neighbourhood lemma, then restriction to D(b), which keeps x' and the étale maps. In the h'=επ'^n normalisation I checked the maps both ways (u0↦ε⁻¹u, inverse u↦εu0); the case h'=0 is handled. The new node lem-sfb-etale-dvr-principal-neighbourhood is true: Spec B is finite since both fibres are finite étale over fields, B_q is a DVR by 0AP2 and going-down, prime avoidance gives D(b) = the primes contained in q, so B[1/b]=B_q, and the flat local map from R is injective. Tested on R, R×R, R×Frac R and Frac R (where the hypothesis fails). It is not a duplicate of lem-sbc-etale-trait-stalk, lem-sbc-etale-trait-section-lift or lem-sbc-trait-etale-extension, and it does not restate a clause of the item. Batch 5: I recomputed the closure from both targets with and without the item's proof. lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model (0CBY) and lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth (056V) are both already in it without the item, are generic geometry, and reach no thm-trf node or nt-assume leaf. The only node the item's proof adds is the new sfb node, so both flags are accepted. No SGA is used. Maintainer note: the existing node lem-sfb-trait-nodal-etale-dvr-model (NU, unsplit) restates this item's 0CDD content plus the smooth-generic n≥1 refinement; the two existing nodes should be merged. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_dvr_nodal_etale_local_form (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec R) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (hf : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R), IsReduced (pullback (C := Scheme) f g) ∧ (pullback (C := Scheme) f g).IsPureDimension 1 ∧ ∀ z : pullback (C := Scheme) f g, IsClosed ({z} : Set (pullback (C := Scheme) f g)) → ¬ ((NodalFiber.projection f Ω g).stalkMap z).hom.FormallySmooth → Nonempty (NodalFiber.completedLocalRing z ≃+* NodalFiber.powerSeriesQuotient Ω)) (x : X) (hx : f x = IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) : ∃ (R' : CommRingCat.{u}) (_ : IsDomain R') (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R') (φ : R →+* R') (π a : R') (U : Scheme.{u}) (p : U ⟶ X) (q : U ⟶ (StrictSemistableModel.nodal a).scheme) (x' : U), Function.Injective φ ∧ IsLocalHom φ ∧ Etale (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) ∧ Irreducible π ∧ (a = 0 ∨ ∃ n : ℕ, a = π ^ n) ∧ Etale p ∧ Etale q ∧ p x' = x ∧ p ≫ f = q ≫ (StrictSemistableModel.nodal a).baseMap ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)
